name: model
summary: A glTF model fitted into the element, lit, turnable and recolored from markup.
looks: The model from `src` sits centered in the box, lit by a soft studio environment and tone mapped like a product shot, facing the viewer or resting in a three-quarter view seen slightly from above. From that pose it can turn on its own, follow scroll, lean toward the pointer and spin under a drag with a little inertia, staying where the visitor leaves it. A part of it takes the color picked in a group of swatches, blending smoothly to the new one.
target: any element; put a poster inside, it shows without WebGL and until the model is ready

params.name: src
params.description: URL of the GLB or glTF file.

params.name: part
params.description: Material or mesh names to recolor, comma separated; empty keeps the file's colors.

params.name: color
params.description: Color of the part, any CSS color.

params.name: swatches
params.description: Selector of a radio group or <select> whose pick recolors the part, as `color` does.

params.name: duration
params.description: Time a color or rest pose change takes.

params.name: scale
params.description: Size in the box: 1 fits the model as it is seen in its rest pose, its near side larger in perspective, centered on what is drawn.

params.name: yaw
params.description: Rest pose turn around the vertical axis; positive turns it as a drag to the right does.

params.name: pitch
params.description: Rest pose tilt toward the viewer; positive shows it from above, -20 to 20.

params.name: spin
params.description: Turns on its own around the vertical; 0 stands still.

params.name: turn
params.description: Turns as the element passes through the viewport.

params.name: tilt
params.description: How far it leans toward the pointer.

params.name: drag
params.description: Turns it under a drag, and with the arrow keys when it has a tabindex.

params.name: clip
params.description: Clip to loop by name, `*` for the first; step keys alone draw only at each key.

params.name: exposure
params.description: Exposure of the tone mapping.

frames.note: Only while something moves: spin, a clip, drag inertia, the tilt settling, or a color or rest pose blending. A clip whose every track steps from key to key, like the hands of a ticking watch, draws one frame per key on a timer while visible, so a watch at rest costs a frame a second. None at rest without spin and clip.

reducedMotion.note: The rest pose shows; spin, clips, scroll turn and tilt stop, and a new rest pose is taken at once. Dragging, arrow keys and color changes still work: the visitor starts them.

presence.note: Leaves by dithering its pixels away while shrinking to 96%, so its opaque materials never switch to transparent mid-transition.

touch: No tilt, nothing hovers. A finger drags the model only when the element has `touch-action: pan-y` or `none`, otherwise the gesture scrolls the page.

cost.gpu: The model as authored, lit by one prefiltered environment. One own material per material of the file.
cost.memory: Geometry and textures of the file, shared with every instance of the same URL, and the environment map.

name: device
summary: A screenshot or a video shown in a 3D phone, tablet, laptop or browser window.
looks: The picture becomes the screen of a device built in 3D with the proportions of the real one: a phone with its camera island and side keys, a tablet, an open laptop with its keyboard and trackpad, or a browser window with its toolbar. The picture covers the screen, centered across and from the top down. It rests in a slight three-quarter view, lit by a soft studio light, with a soft shadow on the page under it. It leans toward the pointer and can turn as the page scrolls.
target: img, video: the screenshot or screen recording; the box holds the whole device and shows the plain picture without WebGL. A phone or a tablet takes the box aspect within the range of real ones, a laptop screen is 16:10, a browser window 5:4 to 12:5

params.name: frame
params.description: phone with a camera island and side keys, 16:9 to 19.5:9; tablet, 4:3 to 16:10; laptop, open with its keyboard, a 16:10 screen; browser, a window with a toolbar, 5:4 to 12:5.

params.name: color
params.description: Color of the body, any CSS color; the browser toolbar takes it too.

params.name: yaw
params.description: Rest turn around the vertical; negative shows the right side.

params.name: pitch
params.description: Rest tilt toward the viewer; positive shows it from above.

params.name: tilt
params.description: How far it leans toward the pointer.

params.name: turn
params.description: Turns it as the element passes through the viewport.

params.name: radius
params.description: Corner rounding: 1 is the device as made, 0 square.

params.name: shadow
params.description: Density of the shadow on the page.

params.name: scale
params.description: Size in the box: 1 fits the device as it is seen in its rest pose, near parts larger in perspective.

frames.note: Only while it leans toward the pointer, settles, or eases to a new rest pose, plus scroll frames with turn and video frames while a video plays. None at rest.

reducedMotion.note: It rests in its pose: no lean, no scroll turn, and a new pose is taken at once.

presence.note: Leaves by dithering its pixels away while shrinking to 96%, and its shadow fades with it.

touch: Nothing hovers, so it rests in its pose; turn still follows the scroll.

cost.gpu: A few hundred triangles lit by one prefiltered environment, the screen as one texture read.
cost.memory: The picture or the video frame, and the environment map.

examples.title: An app screenshot in a phone
A dashboard in a browser window
A screen recording in a laptop that turns with the scroll

name: book
summary: A cover image made a 3D book that turns to show its spine and opens on hover.
looks: At rest the book faces the viewer, its cover exactly where the image was, with a soft shadow under it. Under the pointer it swings to show its spine and the front cover opens a little over the cream page edges. A drag turns it all the way round to the back cover.
target: img: the front cover; the box is the cover, and without WebGL the plain cover image shows

params.name: style
params.description: hardcover has thick boards over the pages and a rounded spine; paperback a thin flush cover and a flat spine.

params.name: pages
params.description: Page count, which sets the thickness.

params.name: spine
params.description: Spine color or image URL; empty takes the color of the left edge of the cover.

params.name: back
params.description: Back cover image URL or color; empty uses the spine color.

params.name: yaw
params.description: Rest turn; positive shows the spine.

params.name: swing
params.description: Turn under the pointer or keyboard focus.

params.name: open
params.description: How far the front cover opens on hover.

params.name: tilt
params.description: How far it leans toward the pointer.

params.name: drag
params.description: Turns it under a drag, and with the arrow keys when it has a tabindex.

params.name: shadow
params.description: Density of the shadow on the page.

frames.note: Only while it swings, opens, leans, coasts after a drag or eases back; none at rest, and pointer moves elsewhere draw nothing.

reducedMotion.note: It rests facing the viewer: no swing, opening or lean. Dragging and arrow keys still turn it, without coasting.

presence.note: Leaves by dithering its pixels away while shrinking to 96%, and its shadow fades with it.

touch: Nothing hovers. A finger turns the book only when the element has `touch-action: pan-y` or `none`, otherwise the gesture scrolls the page.

cost.gpu: About two thousand triangles with a simple light, no environment map.
cost.memory: The cover, and the spine and back images when given.

examples.title: A hardcover from its cover
A paperback with its own spine and back
A course workbook turned by the arrow keys

name: box
summary: A product box built from pictures of its faces: turn it, tilt it, open its lid.
looks: At rest the front of the box lies exactly where the image was, with a soft shadow under it. Under the pointer the box turns to show its right side and leans toward the pointer; a drag turns it all the way round and tips it to show the top and the bottom. With a motion set, the box also opens on hover: the top flap of a folding carton swings back, the lid of a gift box lifts off, or the tray of a sleeve box slides out, and the box leans forward so the inside shows.
target: img: the front of the box; its aspect is the front of the box, and without WebGL the plain front image shows

params.name: motion
params.description: How the box opens on hover, click or Enter. none stays closed; flap swings the top back on a hinge, as on a folding carton of tea or cosmetics; lift raises a lid over the top fifth, as on a rigid gift box; drawer slides a tray out of a sleeve to the right, as on a box of chocolates or a phone.

params.name: back
params.description: Back face image URL or color; empty prints the front on the back too.

params.name: left
params.description: Left side image URL or color; empty takes the right side picture, else the color of the left edge of the front.

params.name: right
params.description: Right side image URL or color; empty takes the left side picture, else the color of the right edge of the front.

params.name: top
params.description: Top face image URL or color, its top edge toward the back; empty takes the bottom picture, else the color of the top edge of the front.

params.name: bottom
params.description: Bottom face image URL or color; empty takes the top picture, else the color of the bottom edge of the front.

params.name: inside
params.description: Color of the bare board inside an opening box; empty is an off-white board.

params.name: depth
params.description: Depth as a share of the front width, so an 18 × 24 × 6 cm box has 0.33, and 0 a flat card; auto takes it from the side picture, else the top picture, else 0.3.

params.name: yaw
params.description: Rest turn; positive shows the right side.

params.name: pitch
params.description: Rest tilt; positive shows the top.

params.name: swing
params.description: Turn under the pointer or keyboard focus: 0 keeps it facing the viewer.

params.name: open
params.description: Share of the full opening shown on hover; a click or Enter opens it all the way. 0 keeps it shut.

params.name: tilt
params.description: How far it leans toward the pointer: 0 turns the lean off.

params.name: spin
params.description: Idle turn while nobody touches the box, pausing under the pointer and for 1.5 s after: 0 turns it off.

params.name: drag
params.description: Turns and tips it under a drag, and with the arrow keys when it has a tabindex.

params.name: shadow
params.description: Density of the shadow on the page.

frames.note: Only while it turns, leans, opens, coasts after a drag or eases back, and while spin turns it; none at rest, and pointer moves elsewhere draw nothing.

reducedMotion.note: It rests as posed: no swing, lean or spin, and hover does not open it. A click or Enter still opens it, at once; dragging and arrow keys still turn it, without coasting.

presence.note: Leaves by dithering its pixels away while shrinking to 96%, and its shadow fades with it.

touch: Nothing hovers. A tap opens and closes a box with a motion, unless the image sits in a link or a button. A finger turns the box only when the element has `touch-action: pan-y` or `none`, and tips it only with `none`; otherwise the gesture scrolls the page.

cost.gpu: Six to twenty flat faces with a simple light, no environment map.
cost.memory: The front image, and the pictures of the other faces when given.

examples.title: A carton from its front and one side
A gift box that lifts its lid, turned by the keys
A game box that turns on its own

name: explode
summary: An exploded view of a model: its parts move apart as the section scrolls.
looks: Works on the `model` of the same element. As the visitor scrolls through a sticky section, the parts of the product move apart one after another, the outer ones first, and come back together on the way up, so a page can show what is inside headphones, a watch, a speaker or a chair. The model shrinks a little as it opens so the exploded view stays in its box, and can turn as it opens. Drag, swatches and the rest pose of `model` keep working.
target: an element with the `model` effect: `data-dio="model explode"`, inside a tall `data-dio-section` with a sticky stage

params.name: mode
params.description: radial moves each part away from the center by its own distance; axis stacks the parts in even levels along `axis`, like a watch or a speaker taken apart; extras takes the offsets the modeler wrote as glTF node extras `"explode": [x, y, z]`, in model units.

params.name: by
params.description: What drives it: pin of the sticky section, viewport progress, or `position` alone for a button or a tween.

params.name: pieces
params.description: Node names of the parts to move, comma separated; empty takes the children of the model root (or every node with extras in extras mode).

params.name: axis
params.description: Direction of the axis mode, in model coordinates: x y z.

params.name: spread
params.description: How far the parts move: 1 as the mode lays them out, 0 keeps them in place.

params.name: start
params.description: Progress at which the parts start to move.

params.name: end
params.description: Progress at which they are fully apart.

params.name: position
params.description: How far apart with `by="manual"`: 0 assembled, 1 exploded.

params.name: cascade
params.description: Share of the run by which the parts start one after another, outer ones first.

params.name: twist
params.description: Turns around the vertical while it opens; 0 does not turn.

params.name: ease
params.description: Time the parts take to catch up with the scroll; 0 follows it exactly.

params.name: contain
params.description: Keeps every part inside the box at every step: the model shrinks and recenters as it opens, measured in its rest pose and in perspective.

frames.note: Only on scroll, and while the parts catch up with it for `ease` seconds; none at rest.

reducedMotion.note: The exploded view stands still, parts apart and without the turn, wherever the page is scrolled. With `by="manual"` the parts jump to `position` without easing.

presence.note: Nothing of its own: the model leaves by dithering, with its parts where they are.

touch: Scroll drives it, so touch works as on desktop.

cost.gpu: None of its own: the model draws as it does without it.

examples.title: Speaker taken apart in a sticky section
Offsets from the model file
A button opens it

name: hotspots
summary: Feature callouts pinned to points of a model, real buttons that follow it as it turns.
looks: Goes on a parent of a `model` element. Its children with `data-dio-at` are lifted out of the flow and follow their points on the model while it turns, is dragged or explodes; a label whose point turns to the back of the model fades out and comes back as the point turns round. Focusing a label, by Tab or a click, turns the model to face its point. The labels stay ordinary buttons or links styled by the page, so keyboard, screen readers and the page without WebGL see a plain list.
target: a parent of the `data-dio="model"` element, holding the labels next to it: the drawn model element hides its own children. Labels get a z-index above a canvas over the page; a sticky stage around them needs one too, or the model covers them (a development note names it)

params.name: model
params.description: Selector of the model element, looked up inside the element and then in the page; empty takes the first `data-dio="model"` inside.

params.name: occlude
params.description: normal hides a point label whose point faces away from the viewer (from the center of the model, or along `data-dio-normal`), and a node label once its part is well behind the center, so exploded parts keep theirs; ray hides a label wherever the model covers its point, for rooms, hollow shapes and parts inside a shell, settling a moment after the model stops; none never hides.

params.name: face
params.description: Focusing a label turns the model to face its point.

frames.note: None of its own: labels move in the frames the model draws, written once per frame as a transform and two custom properties. Card sizes are read once and on resize. Focusing a label draws the turn of the model.

reducedMotion.note: Labels follow the model as it stands; focusing a label turns the model at once, without easing.

presence.note: Labels fade with the model during a page transition.

touch: A tap on a label is a click and turns the model to it; a press on a label never starts a drag of the model.

cost.memory: One empty node per label. With `occlude="ray"`, a ray test against the model for two labels per frame and for all of them once it stops.

examples.title: Feature callouts on a speaker
Room highlights with real occlusion
examples.html:
• Kitchen
  • Balcony

examples.title: Labels on an exploded view

children.description: A point in the model file's own coordinates as x y z (Alt+click on the model logs one in development), or the name of a node whose center the label follows, also while `explode` moves it.
The direction the point faces as x y z, for the normal test; without it, the direction from the center of the model.

Set by the effect to `left` or `right`: the side of the model the label's point is on, where its card goes. With it come `--dio-reach`, px from the point to the near edge of the card, just past the model's edge and inside the element, and `--dio-shift`, px from the point to the middle of the card, so the cards on a side never overlap. The card is the label's last child element, or the label itself; place it with these in CSS.
Set by the effect on a label turned away, which also gets opacity 0; add `transition: opacity 0.2s` to fade it.

name: coin
summary: A coin, medal or token struck from a logo or a photo: it turns, catches the light and flips over.
looks: The image becomes the face of a metal disc with a rim, as thick as a real coin, lying where the image was with a soft shadow under it. A transparent logo is struck into the metal: its shapes stand out in relief, in their own colors or in bare metal, and the field around them is polished metal that mirrors a small studio. A photo of a coin keeps its own look. The coin leans toward the pointer so the light runs over it, turns under a drag to show its edge and its back, and a click turns it over or tosses it so it lands on the other face.
target: img: the front face, the circle in the middle of its box; a transparent PNG or SVG logo, or a photo of a coin cut out round. Without WebGL the plain image shows

params.name: style
params.description: Shape of the object. coin: a thin disc with a narrow rim and a reeded edge, for coins and tokens of crypto and fintech sites; medal: thicker, with a wide polished rim and a smooth edge, for awards and badges; token: a thick enamel token whose edge is striped in metal and white, for loyalty programs and games.

params.name: motion
params.description: What a click or Enter does. flip turns it over about its vertical axis; toss throws it up, tumbling, to land on the other face; none keeps the click for the page.

params.name: back
params.description: Back face image URL or color; empty strikes the front on the back too. A color makes a plain back of that color with the rim.

params.name: metal
params.description: Color of the metal: the rim, the edge and the field around a logo. On a token, the color of its enamel.

params.name: ink
params.description: How much the picture keeps its own colors: 1 prints them, 0 strikes it in bare metal, so only its relief shows.

params.name: relief
params.description: How far the shapes of a transparent logo and the rim stand out: 0 keeps the face flat.

params.name: yaw
params.description: Rest turn; positive shows the right edge.

params.name: pitch
params.description: Rest tilt; positive shows the top edge.

params.name: tilt
params.description: How far it leans toward the pointer: 0 turns the lean off.

params.name: turn
params.description: Turns while the page scrolls past: 360 is a whole turn from entering the viewport to leaving it. 0 turns it off.

params.name: spin
params.description: Idle turn while nobody touches it, pausing under the pointer and for 1.5 s after: 0 turns it off.

params.name: drag
params.description: Turns and tips it under a drag, and with the arrow keys when it has a tabindex.

params.name: shadow
params.description: Density of the shadow on the page.

frames.note: Only while it turns, leans, coasts after a drag, flips, and while spin turns it; none at rest, and pointer moves elsewhere draw nothing. Scroll draws frames only with turn.

reducedMotion.note: It rests as posed: no lean, spin or scroll turn. A click or Enter turns it over at once, without the flip or the toss; dragging and arrow keys still turn it, without coasting.

presence.note: Leaves by dithering its pixels away while shrinking to 96%, and its shadow fades with it.

touch: Nothing leans. A tap flips it, unless the image sits in a link or a button. A finger turns it only when the element has `touch-action: pan-y` or `none`, and tips it only with `none`; otherwise the gesture scrolls the page.

cost.gpu: A disc of about seven hundred triangles; five reads of the picture per pixel of a face for its relief, no environment map.
cost.memory: The front image, and the back image when given.

examples.title: A brand logo struck as a gold coin
An award medal with its back, tossed on a click
A loyalty token that turns with the scroll

name: vinyl
summary: An album cover becomes a record sleeve: the disc slides out and spins.
looks: At rest the sleeve lies exactly where the cover image was, with a soft shadow under it. On hover, once in view or while its player plays, a record slides out of the sleeve to the right and spins at 33 rpm, its grooves catching a sheen of light that stays put while the disc turns. The center label carries the cover or a picture of its own. The sleeve leans a little toward the pointer.
target: img: the cover, the front of the sleeve. Without WebGL, or with reduced motion and a still record, the plain cover shows

params.name: style
params.description: Kind of disc. black: classic black vinyl with grooves; color: colored vinyl in color; picture: a picture disc printed with the label image or the cover; cd: a silver compact disc with the rainbow of its tracks.

params.name: trigger
params.description: What brings the record out. hover: the pointer or keyboard focus, and a click or Enter keeps it out; view: it slides out once the sleeve is well in view and stays; play: it comes out and spins while the player named by for plays, and a click or Enter plays or pauses it.

params.name: for
params.description: CSS selector of the <audio> or <video> for trigger play; empty takes the closest one before the image in its parent, else the first one in the parent.

params.name: label
params.description: Center label image URL or color; empty shows the middle of the cover. With style picture, the image printed on the disc.

params.name: color
params.description: Color of the vinyl with style color.

params.name: out
params.description: How far the record comes out, as a share of its diameter: 0 keeps it in the sleeve, 1 takes it all the way out.

params.name: rpm
params.description: Turntable speed while it spins, in turns a minute: 33, 45 or 78. 0 keeps it still.

params.name: tilt
params.description: How far it leans toward the pointer: 0 turns the lean off.

params.name: shadow
params.description: Density of the shadow on the page.

frames.note: Only while the record slides, spins up or down, and spins; none at rest, and pointer moves elsewhere draw nothing. With trigger play, none while the player is paused.

reducedMotion.note: The record comes out and goes back at once and never spins; the triggers work as usual.

presence.note: Leaves by dithering its pixels away while shrinking to 96%, and its shadow fades with it.

touch: Nothing hovers. A tap brings the record out and back with trigger hover, plays and pauses with trigger play, unless the image sits in a link or a button.

cost.gpu: Two thin discs and a sleeve, a few hundred triangles; the grooves are drawn, not modelled.
cost.memory: The cover image, and the label image when given.

examples.title: An album that shows its record on hover
A record that spins while its track plays
Colored vinyl that slides out in view

name: label
summary: A flat label wrapped around a can, a bottle or a jar that turns to show all of it.
looks: The label image is wrapped around a 3D container standing in the box of the element: printed on an aluminium can, glued on a glass bottle with a foil cap, or around a glass jar with a lid. It keeps its proportions, so its width decides how far around the body it reaches. The container turns as the page scrolls past and under a drag, leans toward the pointer, and the light runs over the metal, the glass and the print.
target: img: the flat label, its whole width as printed; the container stands in the box of the image, as tall as fits. Without WebGL the plain label shows

params.name: style
params.description: Kind of container. can: a 330 ml drinks can, the label printed all around its body, for beer, soda and coffee; bottle: a 750 ml bottle of colored glass with a foil cap, the label on its body, for wine, spirits and oils; jar: a squat glass jar with a twist lid, for cosmetics, honey, coffee and sauces.

params.name: color
params.description: Color of the body: the metal of a can, the glass of a bottle, what fills a jar. Empty takes the default of the style: aluminium, green glass, amber.

params.name: cap
params.description: Color of the cap: the lid of a can, the foil of a bottle, the lid of a jar. Empty takes the default of the style.

params.name: yaw
params.description: Rest turn; 0 shows the middle of the label.

params.name: pitch
params.description: Rest tilt; positive shows the top, as seen from a little above.

params.name: tilt
params.description: How far it leans toward the pointer: 0 turns the lean off.

params.name: turn
params.description: Turns while the page scrolls past: 360 is a whole turn from entering the viewport to leaving it, 180 shows the label from one end to the other. 0 turns it off.

params.name: spin
params.description: Idle turn while nobody touches it, pausing under the pointer and for 1.5 s after: 0 turns it off.

params.name: gloss
params.description: Shine of the light on the print: 0 is matte paper.

params.name: drag
params.description: Turns it under a drag and tips it a little, and with the arrow keys when it has a tabindex.

params.name: shadow
params.description: Density of the shadow on the page.

frames.note: While the page scrolls with turn, and while it leans, coasts after a drag, eases a key step, or spin turns it; none at rest, and pointer moves elsewhere draw nothing.

reducedMotion.note: It rests as posed: no lean, spin or scroll turn. Dragging and arrow keys still turn it, without coasting.

presence.note: Leaves by dithering its pixels away while shrinking to 96%, and its shadow fades with it.

touch: Nothing leans; the scroll turns it. A finger turns it only when the element has `touch-action: pan-y` or `none`, and tips it only with `none`; otherwise the gesture scrolls the page.

cost.gpu: One body of about two thousand triangles with a simple light, no environment map.

examples.title: A can that turns as the page scrolls
A wine bottle turned by a drag
A jar of honey with a gold lid
